frames.narration: A trader sends: buy 200 shares of ACME at up to 10.10, with their own client order id c-88.

The gateway authenticates the connection and runs the risk checks in memory: the account's limit, the price against the last trade, and the order rate. Everything is fine, and the id c-88 has not been seen before.
The sequencer stamps the order with the next number, 1,000,042, and writes it to the journal, on more than one machine, before anything else. Only now is the order official.
The engine and its standby both read order 1,000,042 from the journal. They are deterministic, so both do exactly the same thing with it.

The engine matches in one thread, in memory. The best sell is 100 at 10.05, then 50 at 10.05 further back in the queue, then 80 at 10.10. The buy takes the first two in full, and then 50 of the 80 at 10.10, which fills the whole order. The other 30 shares stay in the book as a sell at 10.10, still first in line.
The engine emits events for the trades and the book changes, each with its own sequence number. The trader is told which orders they traded against.
The same events go to the market data feed, which sends one copy that reaches every subscriber at the same moment, so no firm sees the new prices before the others.
Now the engine's machine fails. The standby already has the identical book, so it takes over from sequence number 1,000,042 within a fraction of a second. No order is lost, and none is matched twice.
